_comment: Source of the generated docs/codemap.md. Entry points are names, never line numbers; suites are class names under src/test. Checked by scripts/render_codemap.py --check.

modules.codec: CBOR with original bytes, exact rationals
modules.crypto: Hashes, signatures, VRF, KES, BLS (jblst, with its start-up check), operational certificates
modules.protocol: Pure Ouroboros mini-protocol codecs and state machines
modules.network: Effectful bearer, multiplexer, connections, peer selection
modules.uplc: Scarab's own UPLC evaluator, the node's only Plutus evaluator (ADR 0027)
modules.plutus: Plutus evaluation through the own evaluator
modules.ledger: Blocks, transactions, rules, native ledger state
modules.consensus: Praos family, chain selection, hard fork, state mirror
modules.storage: Stores, snapshots, migrations, Haskell formats, SCLS, Mithril
modules.models-gen: CDDL parser and Scala generator (build time)
modules.models: Generated CDDL models runtime and equivalence tests
modules.node: The node: wiring, mempool, forging, relay, node-to-client, tools
modules.fuzz: Structured fuzzing of decoder entry points (test only)
modules.tools: Programs run by hand, never as tests and never shipped: benchmarks, probes against a live peer, and the writers of committed fixtures and goldens; they use the modules' test kits
modules.warts: The design rules' own WartRemover warts, compiled against this Scala version's WartRemover and loaded by every module's compiler: build tooling, never shipped

packages.responsibility: aeson's Value with Scientific numbers, Text keys, its Eq, Ord and Show; unused strict native raw JSON Value parser with original-token validation and the reference's error texts
CBOR with original-bytes preservation, document index, exact rationals, base domain error
Blake2b hashing and transaction ids
BLS12-381 min-sig keys, signatures and the Leios committee certificate; the start-up check of the jblst native library
Sum6 KES verify, sign and evolve
Operational certificate decoding and checks
VRF draft-03 verify and prove, Praos leader threshold
Strict Ed25519 witness verification
Pure mini-protocol codecs and state machines, versions, era and header tags
bearer and the node-to-node TCP sockets, multiplexer, connection manager, client and server roles of each mini-protocol
Genesis rate limiting primitives: leaky bucket, limit on patience, picosecond clock
Pure peer selection: governor state, churn, ledger peers, local roots, GSM, CSJ, fetch policy

Plutus data, execution units, language and cost-model parameter names; the term model (builtins with tags and type schemes, constants, terms with Traverse, stack-safe recursion schemes), semantics variants and availability of the own evaluator, with its decoder, machine, builtins and costing as they land

BLS12-381 constants of the own evaluator (G1 and G2 points as their compressed bytes, Miller-loop results with jblst's value) and the pure facade over jblst and Bouncy Castle that the builtins compute with

The reference's saturating integer, budgets, cost streams and the machine's step costs; the cost model: costing-function shapes of each semantics variant, argument measures, the costing of every builtin and the evaluation context from an on-chain cost-model list
The contract between the machine, the builtins and the costing: unlifting, denotations, costing functions and a saturated application in the reference's order

The unlifting of every builtin under variants A to G with each variant's bounds, and the denotations of the core builtins (integers, byte strings, strings, Bool, unit, trace, pairs, lists, Data and its CBOR serialisation)

The CEK machine of the own evaluator: a pure tail-recursive loop over the reference's transitions, values and their discharge, the skew-binary environment, counting and restricting budgets with the slippage, the caser of built-in constants, typed machine errors and the cats-mtl boundary

The denotations of the hashes, the Ed25519, ECDSA and Schnorr verifications, the BLS12-381 builtins, the conversions and bitwise builtins, expModInteger, the Value builtins, the arrays and batch 7, with their typed failures and the reference's log lines

Script bytes to a program: the Flat decoder of programs, terms and constants with every refusal of the reference, and the ledger's deserialiseScript with its predicates, the remainder rule and the version check for evaluation; and the Flat encoder of programs, the inverse of the decoder

The textual syntax of UPLC as plutus 1.70.0.0's parser reads it: programs, terms, types, constants and data with names resolved to de Bruijn indices, Haskell's character escapes and the BLS12-381 point literals; the node itself never reads text

The ledger's evaluation of a script: mkTermToEvaluate (the arguments, the program's version, the scope check), the evaluation context of machines per variant, evaluateScriptRestricting and evaluateScriptCounting with the V3 unit rule, the per-language entry points (PlutusV4 evaluated as PlutusV3), total in the protocol version, and no verdict for a defect of this evaluator

Script evaluator algebra and its interpreter over the own evaluator (uplc), the one backend of the rules, the mempool and the forger; re-exports PlutusData, ExUnits, PlutusLanguage and ParamNames from uplc
Blocks, headers, transactions, governance, parameters, scripts, ledger view and the closed error vocabulary
Byron ledger: transactions, delegation, update, parameters, transport
Decoding of Dijkstra transactions at decoder version 12, in the block and the mempool form, as the Leios testnet's build reads them, and the predicate failures of the Dijkstra rules

Era-specific transaction types (#85): the type families as match types, the reference's era classes with one instance per era, what the eras share (output and script representations, certificate parts), the protocol parameters as higher-kinded data, and the governance state with its classes, read from and written to the node's flat record
Allegra's own types: its output and native script, opaque outside their file
Babbage's own types: its native, Plutus and script types and its output, opaque outside their file

Conway's own types: its native, Plutus and script types and its output, opaque outside their file, with their translations from Babbage; its protocol-parameter record; its certificate, purpose, witness set, auxiliary data, body and transaction, made by its decoders

Dijkstra's own types, of the Leios testnet's build (cardano-ledger 9df9f98c): its native script with the guard, its Plutus script of four languages, its script and its output, read as the build's block decoder reads them, with their translations from Conway; its protocol-parameter record with Leios's and Peras's parameters, the field types it adds, and its class of the parameters
Mary's own types: its output and native script, and their translations from Allegra, opaque outside their file

The reference's rule predicates on the era types, each generic in its era over the reference's classes, in objects named after the reference's Rules modules; their verdicts are compared with the flat rules' (#85, stage 2)
Pure native streaming JSON mechanism for genesis injection files; file/hash wiring remains separate
MemPack TxOut codec and canonical CBOR used by the Haskell snapshot layout

Shelley to Conway rule interpreter: LEDGER, UTXO, BBODY, epoch, tick, rewards (with `MuslMath`, the release node's musl `log`, `pow` and `exp`), governance; Dijkstra's BBODY, LEDGER, UTXOW, UTXO, CERT, POOL and GOV, reached from tests only
Era-indexed native ledger state: UTxO, accounts, certificates, snapshots, vocabulary, diffs
Praos, TPraos and PBFT, chain selection, hard-fork triggers, header rules, volatile chain
Genesis density and diffusion punishment
The Leios build's endorser-block fetch decision: the fetch state, the decision over the peers' offers, the closure's jobs and the reference's StdGen it draws them with
Extended ledger state, chain-dependent state, era history, telescope, state mirror
Immutable, volatile, UTxO and ledger snapshot stores, the Leios endorser-block store, derived codecs, format migration
Reader and importer for the Haskell ImmutableDB layout
Codecs for the Haskell ledger-state file, tables and metadata, and the reference's encoders of the Conway transaction and block parts
The import and export of a Leios reference node's SQLite LeiosDB into and from the Leios store
Certified Mithril snapshot client and bootstrap
SCLS binary import and export of the ledger state
Runtime for CDDL generated models: codecs, writer, decode errors
CDDL parser, schema and Scala emitter run at build time
Node wiring: config, setup, follower, block pool, fetch coordination, governors, header gate, Main
Antithesis assertions from inside the node: the typed capability, its closed catalogue of properties, the fallback SDK's lines and the recording interpreter (--assertions-file)
Block production: leadership, the leader schedule, hot keys, KES files, block builder, forger
Typed node log events, rendering, routing and severity
Mempool state, capacity, its watcher on the chain's tip, local submission and monitor
Prometheus metrics: catalogue, collectors, exposition, event metrics
Node-to-client queries: query decoding, answers, versions, failure CBOR
Read-only projections of ledger state by era for queries
Serving the chain to downstream peers
Command-line tools: SCLS, Mithril, Haskell import, snapshot export and import, captures
